geometry_edits.rationale: Recast the dominant mass as a profiled sectioned volume instead of a purely split bar, to better support the program and portfolio-balanced folded principle.
Use a folded section family to create a clearer inhabitable roof/section relationship without erasing the dominant bar gesture.
Keep the long axis aligned with the existing linear massing so the edited section remains legible in all four views.
Add a public courtyard wrapper to deepen the central void and make the access-edge response more legible as usable ground space.
Size the courtyard as a bounded, program-supporting public void rather than a decorative cut.
Open the court toward the verified access side in the program frame so the public threshold aligns with the street edge.
Promote the courtyard-wrapped mass to root so the new public void becomes the dominant organizing move while preserving the original solid in its ancestry.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the split-wing emphasis with a cleaner folded-section massing rule to better support the neighborhood-living brief and improve sectional continuity.
Widen the central opening slightly so the void reads as a deliberate public seam rather than a narrow split.
Strengthen the ground-level connective mass so the street edge feels anchored and publicly usable.
Slightly lower the upper split mass to reduce the stair-step read and improve the calm upper hierarchy.

rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant split bar with a carved central seam, which gives it a plausible neighborhood-building threshold and a recognizable public void in multiple views. The ground response near the access edge is present but not especially forceful, so the void/publicness score is moderate rather than strong. However, the section is not yet convincing as a clear program-bearing neighborhood building: the form is mostly a low rectilinear extrusion with a split, and the roof/section do not strongly express the requested calm upper hierarchy or any folded/publicly inhabitable section logic. The silhouette is coherent but remains close to a generic bar plus subtraction rather than an integrated stepped/folded mass. Overall the mass is usable, but it needs a stronger sectional program move and a cleaner active-edge response.

warnings: The visible mass appears coherent in plan views, but the section language is weak for a five-floor neighborhood-living brief.
The access-edge response is legible but muted; a more explicit court/notch or entry seam would better satisfy the public-threshold invariant.
The stepped/roof condition currently reads as incidental surface articulation rather than a program-bearing section.
